findings.statement: Future patients may benefit from longitudinal knowledge, but the incremental value of further untreated observation is uncertain.
Future public trust in research institutions can be damaged when institutions knowingly exploit participants or hide material information.
Known feasible alternatives can preserve existing data and some follow-up without imposing the same ongoing harms.

principle_assessments.reason: The relevant future interest is primarily public-health knowledge and institutional trust rather than ecological impact; future benefit does not require continued untreated exposure.
Future benefits cannot fairly be purchased by forcing avoidable burdens onto low-power present participants.

information_requests: What scientifically useful follow-up remains possible after treatment and informed consent?
alternatives_or_safeguards: Preserve existing data; continue only consensual treated follow-up if independently justified.
evidence_that_could_change_view: Evidence that no less harmful way can preserve an urgent major future benefit would strengthen the benefit case but would not erase informed-consent and basic-standing constraints.
